betterquesting:10.desc:8:
The world ended a long time ago. You have nothing - no tools, no food, no clean water.

These quests are §eonly a guide§r: there are no rewards, and nothing here is required. Follow them to learn how this pack works, or ignore them and explore.

§eTips§r
- Open this quest book any time with the §e`§r key (left of §e1§r; change it in Controls).
- Look up any item with §eR§r (recipe) / §eU§r (uses) in the item list.
- The §eStaying Alive§r chapter runs in parallel: water, food, shelter and dangers.
- The first day is short. §eFire, water, light and walls§r before sunset matter more than anything else - see §eThe First Night§r.

Small rocks lie on the ground almost everywhere - pick them up.

Rocks are your first building material and your first weapon: you can §ethrow§r them at things that come too close. Mining stone with weak tools also gives rocks instead of cobblestone.

§eSticks§r drop from leaves (any tree, including the Biomes O' Plenty ones) - break them by hand.
§ePlant Fibers§r come from breaking tall grass and other grassy plants.

You cannot punch trees in this world: logs only come off with an axe. Make one first.

Fresh plant fibers are too green to burn or twist. §eDried Plant Fibers§r are the base of twine, tinder, fiber torches and fire starters.

- Dry grass - §edead grass, desert grass, dune grass§r in dry biomes - drops them directly.
- Any tall grass drops one now and then.
- A §eCrude Drying Rack§r (2 sticks over 2 plant fibers) dries fresh fibers. It works faster in the sun, in warm dry biomes and next to a campfire.
- One straw splits into two dried fibers.

Rocks + a stick + plant fibers make crude tools. They are weak and break fast, but you will want all three:

- §eCrude Axe§r: the only way to get your first logs.
- §eCrude Pickaxe§r: starts you on stone.
- §eCrude Shovel§r: digging gravel with a shovel finds §eflint shards§r.

Chop a tree with your axe. §cTrees fall when you cut them§r - logs come crashing down, so step aside or you may get hit.

Logs fuel everything in the primitive age: campfires, kilns, charcoal.

Put §eany log + your axe§r into your inventory grid to make a §eChopping Block§r (the axe takes a little damage and comes back), then place it on the ground.

§eUse:§r right-click a §elog§r onto it and hit it with your axe (left-click) until it splits into §eplanks§r; a plank on the block splits into §eslabs§r. Better axes split faster and give more.

The block wears down with use - keep a spare log. §eIf nothing happens, you are too hungry§r - eat something.

The Worktable is §ea wooden slab on top of a log§r (inventory grid) - split a log into planks and a plank into slabs on the §eChopping Block§r.

§eUse:§r right-click the worktable to lay out a 3x3 recipe, then §ehit it with a hammer§r until the item is done. You also need a §eCrude Hammer§r: rocks + a stick + plant fibers. There is no vanilla crafting table until iron (see §eA Real Crafting Table§r).

§7A wooden worktable breaks after about 64 crafts - keep the materials for a new one. The stone worktable later barely wears.§r

Sharper tools need §eflint shards§r or §ebone shards§r (either one works).

- Flint shards: dig gravel with a shovel.
- Bone shards: break bones on an anvil, or find them in fossils.
Skeletons drop bones - but at night you have bigger problems than skeletons.
Twist §e3 dried plant fibers§r into §e3 twine§r (inventory grid). Twine ties tools together, builds drying racks and knives, and lashes the better tools.

Nothing burns in this world unless you light it yourself. You need a fire starter:

- §eFlint and Tinder§r: a flint shard + dried plant fibers + a rock. Cheap, wears out quickly.
- §eBow Drill§r: a bow + a stick. Lasts much longer, but a bow needs string.

§eUse:§r aim at tinder, a kiln or a log pile and §ehold right-click§r until it catches. With an unlit torch in your other hand it lights the torch instead.

A campfire in four steps:

1. Craft §eTinder§r: 2 dried plant fibers + 2 sticks.
2. Place the tinder on the ground.
3. Right-click it with §elogs§r to add fuel.
4. Light it with your §efire starter§r.

§eCook:§r right-click raw food onto it and take it off when it is done - §efood left on too long burns§r. Add logs to keep it going. It also boils dirty water bottles, keeps you warm and speeds up nearby drying racks; resting beside it at night heals you. Rain or a bucket of water puts it out; clear the ash with a shovel.

Shards + sticks + twine, crafted on the §eWorktable§r. Flint or bone tools last much longer than crude ones and can mine iron ore. Make a pickaxe, an axe and a shovel.

§7Note: there are no hoes until you have steel - farming is not a primitive-age option.

Drying racks dry plant fibers, wheat (into straw) and food, and can store items.

- §eCrude Drying Rack§r: 2 sticks over 2 plant fibers, holds one item.
- §eDrying Rack§r: sticks lashed with twine around a ladder, holds four.

§eUse:§r right-click items onto the rack and take them off when they look dry. They dry faster under open sky, in warm dry biomes and next to a campfire - and stop in the rain.

Two dried plant fibers tied with a piece of twine make §eStraw§r; four straw pack into a §eStraw Bale§r (thatch).

Straw is the fuel bed of a pit kiln, and a straw bed is the cheapest place to sleep.
Dig clay in rivers, swamps and lakes. Lumps of clay become bricks, buckets and - most importantly - §erefractory bricks§r for the bloomery.

Your first furnace. The kiln itself is §e2 dried plant fibers§r.

1. §eDig a pit§r one block deep: the kiln needs §esolid, non-flammable blocks below it and on all four sides§r (dirt, stone - not wood). The top stays open.
2. Place the kiln and right-click the items to fire onto it (up to 8 of one kind).
3. Add a §estraw bale§r, then §e3 logs§r.
4. Light it with your §efire starter§r and wait.

When the fire goes out, break the ash for the results - some items crack and fail. §cRain ruins a firing§r, so do not fire in bad weather.

It fires clay into bricks, cobblestone into stone and smelts §ecopper ore§r.

§ePolished granite§r on top of a §esmooth stone slab§r.

§eUse:§r right-click an item onto the anvil and hit it: with a §epickaxe§r to split (rocks, stone bricks, slabs), with a §ehammer§r to crush and forge (shards into dust, limestone, blooms). The anvil wears down with use.
§7Optional.§r Stone tools are a solid upgrade over flint and bone, and the stone hammer works the anvil faster.

Each is §e7 Masonry Bricks blocks§r around a core, with a masonry brick on top - the kiln is built around a §epit kiln§r. Not optional: only the §eStone Kiln§r fires §erefractory bricks§r, §equicklime§r and §eglass§r, so the road to iron runs through it.

- §eStone Kiln§r: everything the pit kiln does, faster and with fewer failures.
- §eStone Oven§r: cooks and dries without burning anything.

§eUse:§r right-click the item into the top, fuel (logs, charcoal) into the bottom, and light the opening at the bottom with your fire starter. Take the results from the bottom. A bucket of water puts it out and saves fuel.

Collect §egranite rocks§r (the pink ones) and pack eight of them around a §eclay lump§r: §eCobbled Granite§r. Fire it in the pit kiln into §eGranite§r, then put four granite together for §ePolished Granite§r - the top of your granite anvil.
Five stone rocks around a §eclay lump§r make a §eCobblestone Slab§r. Fired in the pit kiln it turns into a smooth §eStone Slab§r - the base of your granite anvil.

Stone work, step by step:

1. §eCobblestone§r: eight stone rocks around a clay lump.
2. §eStone§r: fire the cobblestone in the pit kiln.
3. §eStone Bricks§r: four stone in a square.
4. §eStone Brick Slabs§r: place the bricks on the granite anvil and hit them with a pickaxe.
5. §eMasonry Brick§r: split a slab on the anvil the same way.

Masonry bricks are what stone tools and machines are made of.

Not quite. Put a §eMasonry Brick§r on the granite anvil and split it with a pickaxe: four §eStone Rods§r. A wooden stick would char in the heat of a bloom - every pair of tongs is built on stone rods.

A §ePit Burn§r turns wood into charcoal (and tar):

1. Craft §elog piles§r (9 logs each) and fill a pit with them - §ecompletely full§r, and not too big.
2. Cover every side with dirt or stone except one pile, light that one with your fire starter and §ecover it at once§r.
3. Wait until the §esmoke stops§r - do not open it early or it burns to ash.
4. Uncover it and break the piles for charcoal.

Charcoal is the bloomery's fuel. It also makes water filters.

The last steps to a bloomery:

1. Split each §eRefractory Clay§r into 4 lumps (inventory grid).
2. Two lumps side by side make an §eUnfired Refractory Brick§r.
3. Fire them in the §eStone Kiln§r - about 1 in 20 cracks.
4. Four refractory bricks in a square make a §eRefractory Bricks§r block.

The bloomery takes §e7 blocks: 28 bricks§r. 15 refractory clay make 30 unfired bricks - two spare for the kiln; if more than two crack, one more batch of refractory clay covers it.

§eShopping list for one bloomery§r
- §e15 clay balls§r (60 lumps): 12 for refractory clay, 3 melted into liquid clay
- §e7 limestone rocks§r (one limestone block) and a bucket of water
- §e1 flint shard§r
- §e6 ash§r

Iron ore needs at least a flint, bone or stone pickaxe.

§eScavenging tip:§r iron found in ruins is mostly ore too - nobody left neat ingots lying around.

A fresh bloom is glowing-hot iron. §cHolding it with bare hands burns you.§r Carry tongs: three flint or bone shards on two §estone rods§r.

§eUse:§r right-click a bloom with the tongs to pick it up. With tongs in either hand, a bloom you take from the bloomery goes into them safely.

Seven §erefractory brick blocks§r in a U shape.

§eUse:§r right-click §eiron ore§r and fuel (§echarcoal§r is best) into the top and light the top with your fire starter. The more fuel, the faster it works; a §ebellows§r facing it speeds it up when you jump on it.

When the fire on top goes out, take the §eBloom§r - with tongs - and clear the ash with a shovel.

Put the bloom on the granite anvil and hit it with a §ehammer§r, standing close - every few blows knock iron out of it. Hammering is hungry work: if the blows do nothing, eat.

On an anvil it takes about 8 hits; on the ground it takes twice as many, breaks the block below and can start fires. Slag that still holds ore goes back into the bloomery.

You made metal from nothing. The primitive age is almost over.

An §eIron Anvil§r from HBM's Nuclear Tech - the first real machine of the old world. With it you can build the next generation of tools and begin to salvage the ruins for steel.

§eThis is the end of the Primitive age.§r Next: the Scavenger age.

With iron you can finally build a vanilla crafting table - no more hammering every recipe.

1. On the Worktable: §e8 iron ingots§r in a ring make a §eCrafting Table Template§r.
2. Then: the template surrounded by §e8 planks§r makes the §eCrafting Table§r.

Every stone machine is built from §eMasonry Bricks§r blocks: §e4 masonry bricks§r (the small ones you split from stone brick slabs on the anvil) in a square.

A stone kiln, crucible or sawmill takes §e7 blocks§r each - 28 masonry bricks. Set up a steady supply: fire cobblestone, square it into stone bricks, split them on the anvil.

Fire §esand§r in the §eStone Kiln§r - the pit kiln is not hot enough. Some of it cracks into glass shards.

The ruins are full of windows, but §csmashing glass cuts you§r: a §eGlass Cutter§r takes it out whole.

You need §e4 glass§r for a Stone Tank.

§e4 masonry bricks§r in the corners, §e4 glass§r on the sides. A tank stores fluid and keeps it when you break it.

Its real job here: it is the heart of the §eStone Crucible§r. §cHot fluids such as lava break it.§r

A crucible §emelts solids into fluids§r. §e7 masonry brick blocks§r around a §estone tank§r, a masonry brick on top.

§eUse:§r right-click clay into the top - a clay lump melts into a little liquid clay, a §eclay ball into 250 mB§r, a clay block into a full bucket. Put fuel (logs, charcoal) in the bottom and light it. Take the §eLiquid Clay§r out with a bucket - a wooden one is fine, liquid clay is not hot.

A circular blade: §e8 flint shards§r (or 8 bone shards, or 8 diorite rocks) around a §eDiorite§r block.

Diorite comes the same way as granite: §e8 diorite rocks§r (the white ones) around a clay lump make §eCobbled Diorite§r - fire it in the pit kiln.

§e7 masonry brick blocks§r around a §eChopping Block§r, a masonry brick on top. The sawmill is the only way to cut §eBoards§r.

§eUse:§r right-click the §eblade§r into the saw, a §ewooden slab§r into the top, fuel (logs, charcoal) into the bottom, and light it. Slabs come out as boards. No blade, no boards.

You need §e4 boards§r for a Soaking Pot.

§e4 boards + 4 masonry bricks§r. The pot soaks things in a fluid.

§eUse:§r pour the fluid in with a bucket, right-click the items into the top and wait. Some recipes need a lit campfire under the pot - the ones on the road to iron do not.

It makes §eFlint Clay§r and §eSlaked Lime§r, and later washes and tans hides. §cHot fluids crack it.§r

Put a §eflint shard§r on the granite anvil and hit it with a §ehammer§r: one shard gives §e3 Crushed Flint§r - exactly what a bloomery's 3 flint clay need.

A §eflint, bone or stone hammer§r (2 shards or masonry bricks, 2 sticks and twine) works much faster than the crude one - and you will want it for the bloom too.

Fill the soaking pot with §eliquid clay§r from the crucible and put in §ecrushed flint§r. Each piece soaks up 250 mB - a quarter bucket - into a ball of §eFlint Clay§r.

One flint clay goes into every batch of refractory clay: make three. That is §e750 mB of liquid clay - 3 clay balls§r melted in the crucible (single lumps give only 62 mB each).

§eLimestone§r is a pale stone found almost everywhere underground.

Break it down with a hammer on the granite anvil: a limestone block becomes cobbled limestone, that becomes §e8 limestone rocks§r, and each rock becomes one §eCrushed Limestone§r.

A bloomery needs 6 quicklime; §e7 crushed limestone§r leaves one spare for the kiln - one block of limestone covers it.
Fire §ecrushed limestone§r in the §eStone Kiln§r, one quicklime each. About 1 in 20 burns to ash instead. The pit kiln cannot do it - this is the other reason the stone kiln is not optional.

Soak §equicklime§r in §ewater§r in the soaking pot: 125 mB each, so a bucket does eight. Out comes §eSlaked Lime§r - the binder of refractory clay.

A bloomery takes §e6§r (750 mB of water).

Fires leave §eAsh§r behind. Collect it from burnt-out campfires (break the ash with a shovel), charcoal pit burns and kilns instead of throwing it away.

Refractory clay needs §e2 ash§r per batch - §e6§r for a bloomery.

On the Worktable: §e4 clay balls§r in the corners, §e2 ash§r above and below the middle, §e2 slaked lime§r left and right, §e1 flint clay§r in the middle - §e5 Refractory Clay§r.

A clay ball is 4 lumps of clay. A bloomery takes §e3 batches = 15 refractory clay§r: 12 clay balls, 6 ash, 6 slaked lime and 3 flint clay.

Animals do not drop meat and leather here. When they die they leave a §eCarcass§r - pick it up, place it on the ground and work it with a knife (shards + sticks + twine, on the Worktable). Either knife works; the carcass gives up its meat, pelts and bones a piece at a time.

§eWhat animals give§r (§alarge hide§r = good for a canteen):
- §eCow§r: beef, §alarge pelt§r, bone shards, lard
- §ePig§r: porkchop, §alarge hide§r, bone shards, lard
- §eSheep§r: mutton, §alarge pelt§r (shear it for wool + a hide)
- §eHorse / Donkey§r: §alarge pelt§r, bone shards, lard
- §eLlama§r: §alarge pelt§r (shear it for wool)
- §eWolf§r: §alarge pelt§r, bone shards, lard
- §ePolar bear§r: §alarge pelt§r, lots of lard
- §eMooshroom§r: §alarge pelt§r (less often), bone shards, lard
- §eRabbit§r: meat, rabbit's foot, §csmall hide§r (no good for a canteen)
- §eBat§r: §csmall pelt§r only
- §eChicken§r: meat and feathers, no hide

Pelts do not drop every time. On a §eButcher's Block§r the knife matters: a §eButcher's Knife§r doubles the meat but usually ruins the pelt, a §eHunter's Knife§r doubles the pelts but usually taints the meat.

Butchering is hard work: §eif nothing happens, you are too hungry§r.

Get a §elarge pelt or hide§r from a cow, pig, sheep, horse, donkey, llama, wolf, polar bear or mooshroom (see §eHunting and Butchering§r).

A canteen takes §e3 hides§r, so plan on three animals - or use a §eHunter's Knife§r on a §eButcher's Block§r to get more pelts out of each carcass.

§7Sheep and llama pelts can be sheared first: you keep the wool and still get a hide to scrape.§r

A §eHunter's Knife§r (shards + sticks + twine, on the Worktable - shaped like a blade, not a cleaver) scrapes the hair and fat off a pelt.

Put the §epelt + Hunter's Knife§r in a crafting grid: out comes a §eScraped Hide§r and the knife takes a little damage.

§7Rabbit hides and bat pelts give small hides - those make leather straps later, not canteens.§r

Scraped hides must be washed before they are any use. Three ways:

- §eFast:§r craft a §escraped hide + a bucket of water§r (the bucket comes back empty).
- §eSlow:§r throw the scraped hide into water and wait - it takes about ten minutes.
- §eLater:§r soak it in a §eSoaking Pot§r of water over a campfire.

You need §e3 washed hides§r for a canteen.

§e3 planks + 1 plant fiber§r on the Worktable. Your first way to carry water:

- §eWash hides§r instantly (next quest).
- §eWater for the night:§r carry a bucket home and pour it out inside your shelter. You can drink from it with an empty hand all night - drinking does not use the water up.

§7A wooden bucket is not built to last: it can be emptied about 8 times, and a full bucket takes damage every second you carry it - fill it near where you need it. If it breaks, it spills its water on the spot.§r

§7Water only refills itself in rivers and oceans. Elsewhere a pond you take water from shrinks, so do not empty your only source.§r
§cWasteland water is too toxic to carry. Never put anything hot in a wooden bucket.§r

A charcoal pit burn also sweats out §eWood Tar§r - if something catches it.

Build a §eStone Collector§r (7 masonry bricks in a U) into the floor of the pit, §edirectly under§r the log piles, before you light the burn. The tar runs down into it; when the smoke stops, take it out with a bucket.

Tar waterproofs wood - the barrel you tan leather in is built from it.

Soak wood in tar in the §eSoaking Pot§r. These two need a §elit campfire under the pot§r:

- §ePlanks§r: 125 mB of tar each make §eTarred Planks§r.
- §eBoards§r (from the sawmill): 50 mB each make §eTarred Boards§r.

A barrel and its lid take §e8 tarred boards and 2 tarred planks§r.

§e6 tarred boards§r around a §etarred plank§r make a §eBarrel§r; 2 boards and a plank make its §eLid§r.

§eTannin:§r pour a bucket of water into the barrel, add §e4 leaves§r of any tree and seal it with the lid. After about ten minutes the water has become a bucket of §eTannin§r - enough for two hides.
Soak a §ewashed hide§r in the soaking pot with §e500 mB of tannin§r (half a bucket) - no campfire needed. It takes about ten minutes.

§e3 twine and 4 sticks§r in a checker pattern over §e2 logs§r.

Set it up §eunder open sky§r: a tanning rack only works in daylight.

Right-click a §etanned hide§r onto the tanning rack and leave it in the sun: about ten minutes of daylight turn it into §eLeather§r. A large hide gives one leather; small hides give small leather pieces.

§e2 leather§r, cut into straps and a sheet, make a §eBackpack§r (see Staying Alive).

A §eBellows§r: 2 §eboards§r and a §emasonry brick§r on top, 2 §eleather sheets§r around a §estone rod§r in the middle, 2 §emasonry brick blocks§r at the bottom. Cut a leather sheet from leather with a hunter's knife.

§eUse:§r place it facing a §ebloomery§r or a stone machine (kiln, oven, crucible, sawmill) and §ejump on it§r - every push of air speeds up the fire.

A bellows that pumps by itself: 2 §etarred boards§r and an §eiron ingot§r on top, 2 §estone rods§r around your §ebellows§r, 2 §etarred planks§r and a §eHeavy Cloth§r at the bottom (heavy cloth: 4 wool around a leather make 3).

§eUse:§r right-click a §ecog§r into it and it keeps pumping, speeding up to §ethree stone machines§r around it - no more jumping. Each push wears the cog down; a redstone signal pauses it.

§eCogs:§r 8 sticks around a plank (wood), or 8 rocks, flint shards or bone shards around a stone rod. Harder cogs last longer.

You get thirsty as you move, work and fight. In an emergency you can §edrink straight from a water source§r: look at the water with an §eempty hand§r and right-click.

- Water from normal biomes is §edirty§r: drinkable, but it can give you parasites. Boil or filter it.
- §eSea water§r is salty: it makes you thirstier and sick to your stomach.
- Water in §cwastelands, deserts and nuke craters is toxic§r: poison and radiation with every sip. You cannot even fill a canteen there.
- Standing in the rain and looking up lets you drink rain water.

If you start in the desert, head for green land and a river - then make a canteen.

§7(German: "reusable bottle".)§r

You cannot make glass yet, but the old world left plenty of bottles behind: look in kitchens, houses and chests in ruined towns. Some are still full.

A bottle holds one drink. Fill it at any water, §eboil it on a campfire§r to make it safe, drink, and keep the empty bottle - it is reusable forever.

§7Drained a Nuka-Cola? The bomb-shaped bottle (and any other empty soda bottle) holds water too - after one fill it is an ordinary water bottle.§r

§e3 washed hides + twine§r (on the Worktable) make a §erawhide canteen§r. It holds several drinks - far more than a bottle.

- Fill it by right-clicking water; water from normal biomes is §edirty§r.
- Canteens cannot go on a fire: purify the water with a §echarcoal filter§r.

Tanned leather (6 for a canteen) works too, but comes much later. With iron you can upgrade it to an §eIron Canteen§r that holds more.

Bottles and canteens are how you carry water:

- §eFill§r: right-click water with an empty bottle or canteen. Water from normal biomes is §edirty§r.
- §eDrink§r: hold right-click. A canteen holds several drinks, a bottle one.
- §ePurify§r: boil bottles on a campfire; canteens cannot go on a fire - craft them with a charcoal filter.

§cWasteland water fills bottles with Toxic Water, and canteens refuse it.§r
Put a bottle of dirty water on a §ecampfire§r (or in a stone oven) and it comes back purified and safe.
Canteens cannot go on a fire. Craft a filled canteen with a §echarcoal filter§r to purify it.

A bottle filled in the wasteland comes out as §cToxic Water§r: poison, nausea and radiation.

No campfire or filter can clean it - that needs a chemical plant, far in the future. §eWhen you travel into the wastes, carry your water with you.§r

Dig grassy dirt by hand for §eStrange Tubers§r, and pick berries - freckleberries, wild strawberries and Biomes O' Plenty berry bushes grow in plains and forests.

Food is less filling here than you are used to, and you only heal when you are well fed. Keep an eye on the saturation shown on your hunger bar.

Cook meat from your carcasses on the campfire. Roasted food restores much more than raw food - and raw meat can make you sick. §eFood left cooking unattended burns.§r

Meat is worth the hunt: most food here is far less filling than you remember, but §ecooked meat still fills you like it used to§r and keeps you full for a long time - the best thing to eat before a long day or a night in the shelter. Eat the same meat every time, though, and it fills you less and less.

Ruined cities still hide pre-war food. Cans keep forever: city chests, rail tunnels and old dungeons are your pantry. Every can comes with a winding key.

§7Scratched inside a locker in a rail tunnel:§r
§o"Day 212. Rules of the tin, for whoever finds this.

Beef, tuna, fried chicken, Spam, hotdogs, pizza - eat. Best things left in this world.

Mystery meat, pashtet, yogurt, the 'mushroom' stew, the astronaut tube - eat, don't ask.

Leftovers: somebody's half-eaten dinner. Still half a dinner. Recursion: two bites, and nine times in ten there's another can inside. Eat one, carry the rest, don't think about it.

Canned Fist punches you. Every time. Still food.

Engine oil, diesel, kerosene, napalm, asbestos. The old world sold it as food and it fills you like food. Nothing worse happened to me. Make of that what you will.

§c§oDo not open the Black Hole.§r§o It opens right where you stand. Kowalski opened the Black Hole. We found his boots."§r

Wild gardens grow in many biomes. Break them for vegetables, fruits and seeds.

§7Real farming needs a steel hoe - that comes in the Scavenger age. Until then, gather and scavenge.§r

There are four ways to eat in the primitive age: §eforage§r, §ehunt and cook§r, §escavenge cans§r and §epick wild gardens§r. You have found one - none of them is enough on its own, so use them all.

- §eVariety is life.§r You start with only §e3 hearts§r. Every new kind of food you eat counts, and at 5, 10, 20, 30, 45, 60 and 80 different foods you gain §eanother heart§r - up to 10. A §eFood Book§r (book + carrot) shows what you have and have not eaten yet.
- §eMonotony starves you.§r The same food over and over fills you less each time and takes longer to eat. Mix your meals.
- Food is less filling than you are used to - cooked food is worth far more than raw.
- You only heal while you are well fed.
- Eating next to a campfire at night makes you §eComfortable§r: food goes further, and a big meal gives you §eWell Fed§r (more stamina).

Nights are §cpitch black§r here - no moonlight to see by. Darkness is also where things spawn: light up your camp.

- §eFiber Torch§r: dried plant fibers on a stick. Cheap, but it §eburns up§r over time and the rain puts it out.
- §eStone Torch§r: coal pieces on a stone rod. §eNever burns up§r, but rain can still put it out.

§eCoal pieces§r come from coal ore and from §elignite§r (HBM lignite ore, underground at y 35-60) mined with a pickaxe below iron. Careful: breaking coal or lignite can release poisonous coal gas.

Proper torches that never go out are made from §ecoke§r - coal or lignite baked in HBM's Combination Oven (Scavenger age).

Rocks craft into cobblestone. Build something you can close behind you before your first night.

Mud and straw make §eCob§r - another cheap early building block.

Nobody sleeps through the night here - but a bed still marks home. §eRight-click a bed§r, day or night, to make it your respawn point. A §estraw bed§r is just 3 straw. A sleeping bag does not count: home is where you can defend it.

You will be back there after every death. If the bed is gone, you wake up somewhere random.
Crates, stashes and drawers keep your loot safe. A §eRock Bag§r collects rocks automatically.

§cEvery tenth night a horde comes for you§r - and it grows each time. You cannot sleep through it.

Zombies carrying pickaxes §edig through walls§r. HBM concrete stops them; until you have it, build thick walls, light everything and have an escape route.

Bitten survivors can catch the zombie infection. Watch your status effects.

Night falls fast, and it is darker than you remember. Before the sun goes down:

- §eFire§r: a campfire keeps you warm, cooks, and lets you rest and heal.
- §eWater§r: a full bottle or canteen - you cannot go looking for a river in the dark.
- §eLight§r: torches around your camp; monsters spawn in darkness. Out there the night is pitch black: hold a torch in your offhand and light it with a bow drill or flint and steel in your main hand. A lit torch lights your way until it burns down - and rain or water puts it out.
- §eFood§r: something cooked, something stored.
- §eWalls§r: anything you can close behind you - dig into a hillside if you must.

§cAt the first sunset, watch the western sky.§r Something falls from it - and the parasites come with it. From that night on, the dark is no longer safe. Do not go looking for the crash site tonight: the meteorite's crater is where they breed.

Do not wander at night. Zombies hear noise and follow light, and worse things hunt in the dark. Survive until morning - then do it again.

Damage hits §especific body parts§r: a hurt leg slows you down, a damaged head blurs your sight. Plasters and bandages heal individual parts - look for them in ruins.

Health only regenerates while you are well fed.

Your body temperature matters. Deserts and wastelands are scorching by day and freezing at night; rain and water chill you.

Stay near a campfire at night, wear cloth armour in the cold, and keep an eye on the thermometer on your HUD.

When you die your belongings stay in a §egrave§r where you fell - you respawn with a key to it. Go back carefully: whatever killed you is probably still there.

You lose most of your experience on death, and experience is what buys skill levels.

- §eParasites§r come from fallen §emeteorites§r. Each meteorite is a hive with its own evolution: its parasites start weak, but they grow stronger as they kill, spread and assimilate other creatures - and its zone grows with them. The longer a hive goes unchecked, the worse it gets.
- A hive dies when the §eliving core§r in its crater (the pulsing alveoli and cysts) is destroyed. A young one can be raided with a pickaxe; an old one is far too dangerous to walk into - that is what explosives, and one day nukes, are for. Another meteorite falls a few days later.
- §eMutated wildlife§r roams the wastes - giant worms, insects and worse.
- Some monsters are §eelite§r: a coloured health bar and special powers. Avoid them early.
- Zombies hear noise, see light and follow blood.

Cities stand in ruins - the worst in the wastelands. They are full of loot and full of danger.

- Some buildings are §ehaunted§r: their chests stay locked until you clear the building.
- Concrete and steel walls §ecannot be dug through§r without at least an iron pickaxe - use the doors.
- §cSmashing glass cuts you§r: breaking windows makes you bleed. A §eGlass Cutter§r removes glass safely (and keeps it).
- Watch for radiation, landmines and asbestos dust near old industrial sites.
- Underground rail tunnels hold the best early caches.

Experience buys skill levels (open the skills tab in your inventory). Tools and machines are never locked by skills - but §eweapons and armour are§r: better guns, swords and armour need Attack, Defense or Agility levels.

A backpack worn on your back roughly doubles what you can carry home from a scavenging run.

§e2 leather straps§r on the sides, a §eleather sheet§r at the bottom, an §eiron ingot§r on top and §ewool§r in the middle, with §etwine or string§r in the four corners.

Cut leather with a §ehunter's knife§r: leather makes a sheet, a sheet makes 2 straps - §e2 leather§r in all. Leather is tanned from hides - see the end of the Path to Iron chapter.

§eWear it§r in the §eBody§r slot of the Baubles inventory. You cannot open it on your own back: take it off and §eplace it on the ground§r, then right-click it. Another player can open it while you wear it.

You can make iron. The old world made far more - and left it lying in the ruins.

This age is about §esteel§r, the first §eelectricity§r and the old machines, and it ends with §eoil and plastic§r: everything after (computers, rifles, automation) is built on plastic.

§eTips§r
- Most HBM machines are built on the §eanvil§r: right-click it, pick the recipe, hammer.
- An iron pickaxe breaks the concrete and steel of the ruins; reinforced blocks need steel.
- Look up anything with §eR§r (recipe) and §eU§r (uses) - the machines below have long recipes.

§eOne way to steel:§r take it from the ruins. They are full of steel - rusted, but steel.

Break §erusty steel§r and §esteel deco blocks§r (iron pickaxe) and recycle them on the anvil: §e8 rusty steel or 4 steel blocks give 1 steel ingot§r. Old filing cabinets, tape recorders and satellite dishes give steel too.

No furnace needed - just a lot of walking. The other way is the blast furnace.

§e4 iron ingots, an iron block, a Pyrotech cog§r (stone, flint, bone or iron) and §e3 masonry bricks blocks§r as its firebox. It burns solid fuel.

§eStamps:§r 3 bricks + 3 stone (or iron, or steel) make a §eflat stamp§r; on the anvil you cut it into a §eplate§r, §ewire§r or §ecircuit§r stamp. Put the stamp in the press, fuel below, the metal in - out come §eplates§r (one per ingot) or §ewires§r (eight per ingot).

Iron, copper and steel plates go into almost every machine.

§eFireclay§r is clay tempered with broken pottery: §e3 clay balls + pottery fragments or a pottery shard§r make 4. Fire it in the §epit kiln or stone kiln§r into §eFirebricks§r.

Pottery fragments are what a cracked kiln firing leaves behind - and a cracked fireclay firing leaves more of them for the next batch. For a steady supply, §ehammer clay bricks§r on the granite anvil: a brick gives 1 fragment, a brick block 4.

The blast furnace takes §e32§r firebricks, the crucible 20, molds and foundry channels a few each.

§eThe other way to steel:§r make it. On the iron anvil: §e4 stone bricks, 32 firebricks and 8 copper plates§r.

- §eSteel§r: 2 iron ingots (or 2 iron dust, or 1 iron ore) + sand. Flux instead of sand doubles the steel from ore.
- §eRed copper§r: copper + redstone make 2 - the metal of wires and coils.

Slag comes out as a by-product; keep the outputs clear.

Salvaged or smelted - steel is steel. With §e16 ingots§r in hand the old world's machines are within reach: the steel anvil first.

Salvage is quick to start but runs out where you live; a blast furnace keeps going as long as you have iron.

Copper alloyed with §eredstone§r - the metal of every wire and coil.

- §eBlast furnace:§r a copper ingot + redstone make 2.
- §eCrucible:§r melt copper and redstone together, 1 to 1, and cast ingots.

Press a §ered copper ingot§r with the wire stamp: §e8 red copper wires§r.

- §eCopper coil§r: 8 red copper wires around an iron (or steel) ingot.
- §eCoil torus§r: 4 coils around an iron or steel plate make 2.

On the anvil: §e2 iron plates, a copper coil and a coil torus make 2 motors§r.

Motors drive the assembly machine, the shredder, the derrick and the pack's wood-burning generator.

Put your iron anvil on the anvil's smithing slot with §e10 steel ingots§r: a §eSteel Anvil§r (tier 2).

Tier 2 builds the real machines: firebox, crucible, Stirling engine, assembly machine, soldering station, rotary furnace, boiler.

Steel anvil: §ea Pyrotech stone kiln, 8 steel plates and 8 copper ingots§r.

It burns solid fuel and §eheats the machine standing on top of it§r - the Stirling engine, the crucible, the boiler. HBM's heat machines do nothing without a heat source below.

Three ways to the first electricity:

- §eStirling Engine§r on a firebox (steel anvil: 16 planks, 6 steel plates, 8 copper, 4 coils, a large gear). Cheap, steady.
- §eWood-Burning Generator§r: 5 steel plates, 2 coils, a stone kiln and a motor.
- A §eDiesel Generator§r looted from the ruins - building one needs plastic. It burns liquid fuel.

§eRed Copper Cable§r carries the power: 3 red copper wires + 2 insulators make 16.

Machines need §evacuum tubes§r and §eanalog circuit boards§r.

- §eSalvage:§r old computers, radios and satellite gear break down into circuits on the anvil.
- §eSoldering Station:§r an analog board is 3 vacuum tubes and 2 capacitors soldered onto 4 printed circuit boards with fine lead wire.

Steel anvil: §e8 steel ingots, 4 copper plates, 2 motors and 4 vacuum tubes§r.

§eUse:§r choose a recipe in its menu, put the ingredients in and give it power (100 HE/t). It builds nearly every machine from here on - the shredder, tanks, the derrick, the refinery, the chemical plant.

Assembly machine: §e8 steel plates, 4 copper plates, 2 motors§r. It needs §eshredder blades§r (4 steel plates + a steel ingot) and power.

It grinds ores and items into dust - §ecoal dust§r and §efluorite dust§r for plastic, and doubles many ores.
§eFluorite ore§r is found underground; mining it drops §eFluorite§r. One fluorite goes into every polymer ingot, together with 2 coal dust from the shredder.

Steel anvil: §e20 firebricks, 8 copper ingots, 8 steel plates§r. Stand it §eon a firebox§r.

It melts metals and mixes them into §ealloys§r. Molten metal pours through §efoundry channels§r (2 firebricks + a stone slab) into a §efoundry mold§r holding a §emold§r (blank mold: 4 firebricks + iron, shaped on the anvil) - ingots, plates, gun parts.

§eHigh-speed steel§r (steel + tungsten + cobalt) is made here - the titanium drill needs it.

Assembly machine: §ea triple high-speed steel plate and 8 titanium plates§r.

§eTitanium ore§r is found underground and smelts like iron. High-speed steel comes from the crucible: steel, tungsten and cobalt.

Oil sits in deep pockets underground. An §eOil Detector§r (gold wire, copper, an analog board, steel plates) tells you when you stand above one.

§eOil Derrick§r (assembly machine: steel plates, triple copper plates, steel pipes, a motor and the titanium drill): set it over the deposit and power it. It pumps §ecrude oil§r and §enatural gas§r - pipe them into tanks with universal fluid ducts.

Not plastic - wrapped wool. §e1 wool + 2 twine (or string)§r make §e4 insulators§r.

The ruins have plenty: insulators turn up in chests, and §eRolls of Insulation§r sit in the walls of ruined buildings - each one is 9.

Cables need them (2 per 16 cables), and so do the big machines: the boiler and refinery take 8 each, the chemical plant 16.
The refinery only takes §ehot§r crude oil. A §eLarge Boiler§r (steel anvil: 4 steel ingots, 16 copper plates, 8 insulators) on a §efirebox§r heats crude oil the way it boils water.

Assembly machine: steel plates and shells, copper plates, 12 steel pipes, §e8 insulators and 3 analog boards§r.

It splits hot crude oil into §e50% heavy oil, 25% naphtha, 15% light oil and 10% petroleum gas§r, plus sulfur. Petroleum gas is what plastic is made of; the oils become fuels later.

Assembly machine: 8 steel ingots, 2 copper pipes, §e16 insulators§r, 2 motors, 2 tungsten coils and an analog board.

§eUse:§r choose a recipe, feed it items and fluids (ducts or canisters) and power. It also cleans toxic water, much later.

In the chemical plant: §e2 coal dust + 1 fluorite dust + 500 mB petroleum gas = 1 polymer ingot§r.

You make plastic from oil now - the first truly modern material since the end.

§eThis is the end of the Scavenger age.§r Next: the Industrial age - rifles, computers, storage, automation.
Steel tools and armour (vanilla shapes, steel ingots) outlast iron by far, and a steel pickaxe breaks the reinforced blocks of the ruins.
Only §esteel hoes and better§r can till the soil in this world. With a steel hoe (2 steel ingots + 2 sticks) you can finally plant the seeds from wild gardens - real food that grows back.

- §eSteel Crate§r: 3 steel plates + 5 steel ingots - lots of room, and it keeps its contents when you pick it up.
- §eStorage drawer upgrades§r: x2 capacity with iron plates, x4 with steel plates.

A §eDrawer Controller§r: 3 steel plates on top, comparators either side of a drawer, and steel plates around a §emotor§r below.

Place it touching your wall of drawers: put items into the controller and they go to the right drawer, anywhere in the connected block.

Steel anvil: §e2 triple steel plates, 4 copper coils, 4 tungsten bolts and 2 vacuum tubes§r.

§eUse:§r give it power, choose a circuit, put the parts on top, the circuit board in the middle and solder (fine lead wire) in its slot. It makes the §eanalog circuit boards§r that the assembly machine, the oil detector and the refinery need.

Tungsten bolts: tungsten ore lies deep underground; 2 ingots make 16 bolts.
§e4 steel plates, 2 glass panes, an iron plate§r. With a filter (iron plate + coal filter) it keeps out coal dust, asbestos and the worst of the fallout dust around old industry.

Oil needs somewhere to go.

- §eSteel Barrel§r: 6 steel plates + 2 steel ingots, a portable tank.
- §eTank§r (assembly machine: 8 steel plates, 4 steel shells): a big one.
- §eUniversal Fluid Ducts§r connect them; set the fluid type with a fluid identifier.
§e2 steel plates + a red copper ingot§r. Put a battery in it to store power for the night - a Stirling engine runs only while the firebox burns.

- §eRocks§r can be thrown - right-click.
- The §eCrude Spear§r is thrown too and sticks in what it hits; go and pick it up.

Enough for a rabbit, not for a zombie.
Shards, sticks and twine on the Worktable: §eflint or bone spears and swords§r. The spear still throws and hits much harder than the crude one.
Spartan Weaponry: §ehandles§r (a stick + twine or string) and planks make clubs, daggers, spears and more. The §espear§r is the pick - it reaches further than a sword.

Every Spartan weapon also comes in stone - cut from §emasonry bricks§r. Good picks:

- §eSpear / Pike§r: reach.
- §eWarhammer§r: heavy hits, good against armour.
- §eJavelins and throwing knives§r: damage from a distance.

- §eBow§r (Attack 2): twine works as a bowstring.
- §eWooden longbow and crossbow§r (Spartan): more power, no skill needed.
- §eFlint and bone arrows§r (Pyrotech) hit harder than plain ones.

A bow keeps the horde at arm's length - the safest weapon you will have for a long time.
With bloomery iron: the whole Spartan arsenal in iron, crossbows and longbows included. Needs §eAttack 3§r.

The first gun you can make: §e2 iron ingots, a plank and a copper ingot§r. Attack 4.

It fires black powder loads - paper and gunpowder with §ea ball, flint, an iron ball or gravel shot§r (6 per craft). Gunpowder comes from the ruins.

Techguns: a §estone barrel§r (6 stone), §eflint and steel§r and a §ewooden stock§r (3 logs). Attack 4.

§eStone Bullets§r: 3 masonry bricks + gunpowder make 16. Slow to reload, loud, and it hurts.
HBM steel counts as steel for Spartan Weaponry: the best melee weapons and bows of this age. Needs §eAttack 5§r.
Techguns: §ea steel nugget and 3 steel plates§r. Attack 4. A solid melee weapon - and the classic tool of every scavenger.

The first real guns are simple ones (Techguns), built from steel parts:

- §eRevolver§r (Attack 5): an §eiron barrel§r (6 iron plates), §eiron mechanical parts§r (4 steel plates + flint), §eflint and steel§r and a §ewooden stock§r (3 logs). Fires §ePistol Rounds§r.
- §eSawed-Off§r (Attack 5): 2 iron barrels, 2 flint and steel and a wooden stock. Fires §eShotgun Rounds§r - devastating up close.

§eAmmo:§r Pistol Rounds - 7 copper nuggets + a lead ingot + gunpowder make 8; Shotgun Rounds - 5 copper nuggets + 3 lead nuggets + gunpowder make 5. Lead ore is found underground; gunpowder in the ruins.

§7The Techguns pistol needs space-age parts - until then, only what you find.§r

HBM guns load HBM cartridges. The §eAmmo Press§r (2 iron, a Pyrotech cog, 2 copper, 3 stone) puts a bullet, powder and a casing together - e.g. §e.357 Magnum (black powder)§r: a lead ingot, gunpowder and a casing make 16.

Casings are pressed from gunmetal plates with a casing stamp.

HBM guns are put together from parts in a crafting grid. §eBarrels, receivers and mechanisms§r are §ecast§r: molten steel from the crucible into a foundry mold with the right mold. Grips and stocks are simple: 3 or 4 planks.

Mechanisms are made of §egunmetal§r:
- §eZinc ore§r lies deep underground (below y 37); fire it in the pit kiln or stone kiln into zinc.
- The §eRotary Furnace§r (steel anvil: stone bricks, firebricks, iron, copper plates) melts §e3 copper + 1 zinc§r into gunmetal. It runs on §esteam§r - water boiled in a boiler on a firebox.
A light steel barrel and receiver, a gunmetal mechanism and a wooden grip. Attack 5. It fires §e.357 Magnum§r from the ammo press.

- §eLever Action Shotgun§r (Attack 6): 2 light steel barrels, a steel receiver, a gunmetal mechanism, a steel bolt and a wooden stock.
- §eLever Action Rifle§r (Attack 8): 2 light steel barrels, a gunmetal receiver and mechanism, a gunmetal plate and a wooden stock.

Check what each one loads with §eU§r on the gun.

A heavy steel barrel, a light steel receiver, a gunmetal mechanism and a steel grip. Attack 4.

Not much of a weapon - but a flare lights up the pitch-black night around a horde before it reaches your walls.

Wool in the armour shapes: §eCloth Hood, Jacket, Trousers and Boots§r.

Barely stops a bite - but it keeps you warm. Deserts and wastelands freeze at night, and rain chills you; a full cloth set is what lets you stay out after dark.

Leather armour, two ways:

- §eLeather§r: cut leather into §esheets and straps§r with a hunter's knife (a tunic is 6 sheets + 2 straps).
- §eWoven Cotton§r (HarvestCraft): 2 twine or string make one; 8 make a tunic. No tanning needed.

§7Soak it with 8 slaked lime around it and the leather becomes fireproof. Leather repair kits keep it going.§r
Bloomery iron in the vanilla shapes - 24 ingots for a full set. The first armour that really turns claws and teeth. No skill needed.

§e6 planks around an iron ingot§r. Defense 3.

Hold right-click to block - a zombie's swing or an arrow stops at the shield. In a doorway with a spear in the other hand, it buys you a night.

HBM steel in the vanilla shapes: §e5, 8, 7 and 4 steel ingots§r. Defense 5.

Salvaged steel works as well as smelted.

Techguns' first armour sets, made of §eHeavy Cloth§r (4 wool + 1 leather make 3 - the ruins have it too):

- §eSoldier's§r: heavy cloth with iron plates sewn in (a vest is 5 cloth + 3 iron ingots).
- §eBandit§r: all cloth (a vest is 8).
- §eMiner's§r: cloth and some iron (a jacket is 6 cloth + 2 iron ingots).

Defense 5.

Not armour against teeth - armour against the §ewasteland§r: radiation, fallout and poison.

§eHazmat Cloth§r comes from the assembly machine: 4 lead dust + 8 string make 4. Helmet 5 cloth with a glass pane and an iron plate, suit 8, trousers 7, boots 4. Add a gas mask for the air.

Techguns: a §eshield§r, §e6 steel ingots§r and §e2 glass panes§r. Defense 10.

Big enough to hide behind, with a window to see what is coming. A goal for when your Defense skill catches up.
From empty pockets to your first iron and the first HBM anvil.
Water, food, shelter, health and the dangers of this world.
Steel, the first electricity and the old machines - from the HBM anvil to oil and plastic.

The good weapons of the Primitive and Scavenger ages, and the way to them. Weapons are locked behind Attack levels (bought with experience in the skills tab): wood and stone need none, iron Attack 3, steel Attack 5, the first guns Attack 4 to 8.
